title: Phishing to Domain Compromise — Two-Host Lateral Movement
description: Hand-authored reference recording for Clouseau Live. Depicts a realistic phishing-borne intrusion pivoting from a finance workstation to a domain controller. All IPs use IANA-reserved documentation ranges (TEST-NET-2/3); all hostnames, files, and domains are fictional.

events.narration: Investigation started. Point of interest: domain secure-invoice-portal.com, reported by a finance employee.
The Chief Inspector is reviewing the point of interest and planning the first lead.
Chief Inspector dispatches an Investigator: “Check who resolved or visited secure-invoice-portal.com, and what happened afterward.”

detail.lead: Investigate the domain secure-invoice-portal.com. Find any processes that resolved or visited this address, and any files downloaded around that time.

events.narration: Investigator 1 begins work on host WIN-FINANCE-07.
DNS specialist agent is asked to resolve the domain to its network address.

detail.question: What IP address does secure-invoice-portal.com resolve to?

events.narration: Querying the DNS log table for this domain.

detail.sql: SELECT query, answers, ts FROM dns_logs WHERE query LIKE '%secure-invoice-portal.com%';

events.narration: Result: the domain resolves to 203.0.113.47 — an address not previously seen on this network.
Artifact recorded: suspicious domain secure-invoice-portal.com → 203.0.113.47.
Browser specialist agent checks activity around this domain.

detail.question: Which process visited secure-invoice-portal.com, and what was downloaded?

events.narration: Querying browser history for this domain.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, process_name, url, ts FROM browser_logs WHERE url LIKE '%secure-invoice-portal.com%';

events.narration: firefox.exe (PID 4521) visited the site at 09:14:02 and downloaded “Invoice_July.docm”.
Artifact recorded: macro-enabled file Invoice_July.docm delivered via drive-by download.
Process-audit specialist agent builds the execution tree around the download.

detail.question: What process opened Invoice_July.docm, and what did it spawn?

events.narration: Querying the process table for children of the office process around 09:15.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, ppid, process_name, cmd_line, ts FROM processes_logs WHERE process_name IN ('WINWORD.EXE','powershell.exe') AND ts BETWEEN '09:14:00' AND '09:16:00';

events.narration: WINWORD.EXE (PID 4602) opened the document, then spawned an obfuscated PowerShell command one second later.
Artifact recorded: WINWORD.EXE was hijacked to launch a hidden PowerShell downloader (PID 4718).
Tracing what the PowerShell downloader executed next.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, ppid, process_name, cmd_line, ts FROM processes_logs WHERE ppid = 4718;

events.narration: PowerShell spawned rundll32.exe (PID 4790), which is not a normal child for this process.
Checking network connections made by this process.

detail.question: What network connections did rundll32.exe (PID 4790) make?

events.narration: Querying flow logs for this PID.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, process_name, ip, port, ts FROM flow_logs WHERE pid = 4790 ORDER BY ts;

events.narration: Confirmed beacon: rundll32.exe connects to 203.0.113.47:443 every ~60 seconds starting at 09:16:02.
Artifact recorded: rundll32.exe (PID 4790) is an active command-and-control beacon.
Investigator 1 reports back: confirmed phishing-based initial access via a macro document, with an active PowerShell-launched C2 beacon.

detail.summary: Initial access via secure-invoice-portal.com → Invoice_July.docm. WINWORD.EXE hijacked to spawn powershell.exe (PID 4718), which spawned rundll32.exe (PID 4790), beaconing to 203.0.113.47:443.

events.narration: The Chief Inspector notices the beacon process also made an internal SMB connection — a possible pivot to another host.
Checking for internal (non-internet) connections from the same process.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, process_name, ip, port, ts FROM flow_logs WHERE pid = 4790 AND ip LIKE '10.%';

events.narration: Found an SMB connection (port 445) from this host to the domain controller at 09:42:17.
PIVOT CONFIRMED: WIN-FINANCE-07 → WIN-DC-01 over SMB (port 445), driven by the C2 process. The Chief Inspector opens a second investigation on the domain controller.
Chief Inspector dispatches a second Investigator to WIN-DC-01 with the pivot details.

detail.lead: An SMB connection arrived from 10.10.20.7 (WIN-FINANCE-07) at 09:42:17 to this domain controller. Investigate what happened on this host afterward.

events.narration: Investigator 2 begins work on host WIN-DC-01.
Process-audit specialist checks what ran right after the SMB connection landed.

detail.question: What process activity followed the connection from 10.10.20.7 at 09:42?

events.narration: Querying the process table for the window after 09:42.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, ppid, process_name, cmd_line, ts FROM processes_logs WHERE ts BETWEEN '09:42:00' AND '09:45:00' ORDER BY ts;

events.narration: svchost.exe spawned cmd.exe (PID 2210), which ran domain enumeration commands.
Artifact recorded: attacker enumerated Domain Admins from cmd.exe (PID 2210) immediately after the pivot.
Checking for any new services created around this time (a common persistence technique).

detail.sql: SELECT pid, ppid, process_name, cmd_line, ts FROM processes_logs WHERE cmd_line LIKE '%sc.exe create%' OR cmd_line LIKE '%New-Service%';

events.narration: A new service, “WinUpdateSvc”, was installed at 09:47:30 for persistence.
Artifact recorded: malicious persistence service “WinUpdateSvc” (PID 2255).
Checking what the persistence service did once running.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, ppid, process_name, cmd_line, ts FROM processes_logs WHERE ppid = 2255;

events.narration: The service spawned 7z.exe, which compressed a file share into a single archive.
Artifact recorded: sensitive archive HR_Records_2026.zip staged for exfiltration.
Checking whether this archive left the network.

detail.sql: SELECT pid, process_name, ip, port, SUM(size) AS bytes, ts FROM flow_logs WHERE pid = 2301 GROUP BY pid, ip, port;

events.narration: 340 MB transferred from 7z.exe to external address 198.51.100.23:8443 at 10:12:44.
Artifact recorded: 340 MB of HR data exfiltrated to 198.51.100.23.
Investigator 2 reports back: attacker pivoted to the domain controller, enumerated Domain Admins, installed a persistence service, and exfiltrated HR data.

detail.summary: Lateral movement via SMB from WIN-FINANCE-07. cmd.exe (PID 2210) enumerated domain admins, WinUpdateSvc (PID 2255) installed for persistence, 7z.exe (PID 2301) staged and exfiltrated HR_Records_2026.zip (340MB) to 198.51.100.23:8443.

events.narration: The Chief Inspector reviews both investigation reports and compiles the full two-host attack narrative.

Final report: a phishing email led to macro-based execution on WIN-FINANCE-07, a C2 beacon, lateral movement over SMB to WIN-DC-01, and exfiltration of HR records — fully reconstructed across two hosts.
Evaluating the reconstructed report against ground truth.
Scored against ground truth: precision 0.97, recall 0.94, F1 0.955 across both hosts.
Investigation complete.
